concepts.description: The SRanger system is a small ground robot that travels in a straight line and turns in place when it detects an obstacle.
A single infrared distance sensor mounted facing forward on the robot.
A differential-drive motor pair that accepts a combined linear and angular velocity command.
The reactive controller whose only sensor input is the IR-driven obstacle event and which issues motor commands as advisory events to the differential-drive layer.
An IR-driven obstacle event used as the controller sensor input.
An Actuator interface that records the last motor command.
A small set of state variables, notably a clock-reset timestamp for the timed Turning → Moving transition.
A single state machine that selects transitions based on the input event, the IR distance, and the elapsed time in the current mode.
An operating mode of the SRanger controller.
A fixed configuration constant of the SRanger controller.
The function distance() returns the latest IR distance reading.

instances.description: The SRanger system is a small ground robot that travels in a straight line and turns in place when it detects an obstacle.
The IR-driven obstacle event that forms the controller's only sensor input.
The system-level endTask event available to halt the controller.
Initial mode in which the robot drives forward at the configured linear velocity.
Mode in which the robot rotates in place at the configured angular velocity.
A terminal mode entered when the operator issues endTask.
Linear velocity command when Moving; default 1.0 m/s.
Angular velocity command when Turning; default 2.0 rad/s.
IR-distance threshold for the obstacle-detection condition; default 0.5 metres.
How long the controller remains in Turning before returning to Moving; default 2.0 seconds.
Delivered each control cycle by the system framework.
A combined command to the differential-drive layer carrying a linear velocity and an angular velocity.
Returns a real number in metres, non-negative; returns a large default value when no reading is available.
Records when the controller most recently entered the Turning state; used for the timed Turning → Moving transition.
